components.description: HOP 6-1103: a faculty member on family/medical leave first uses accumulated sick leave; once it is exhausted, the faculty member may resume non-teaching duties at regular salary for the remainder of the 12-week FMLA allotment (teaching relieved), instead of taking the remainder unpaid. Coded as one 12-week relief period under R1e.
components.mechanism_note: R1e names this provision: 12 weeks, sick leave first, then non-teaching duties at regular salary; the employer guarantees regular salary with teaching relieved once own balances are used, so the whole period counts as relief in the relief's category (Just teaching).
components.faculty_group_note: faculty member taking family leave (HOP 6-1103, all UT Arlington faculty)
components.eligible_parent_wording: a faculty member taking family leave; Faculty who are on family/medical leave
components.service_requirement: none stated in HOP 6-1103; the 12-week allotment is the FMLA allotment (12 months of state employment and 1,250 hours, Procedure 3-16)
components.entitlement_note: V2: 'they may: ... Resume non-teaching duties and receive their regular salary' gives the faculty member the choice; the department's decision (with Dean and Provost approval) decides whether the courses must be offered and covered, i.e. the arrangements.
components.duration_note: The relief runs for 'the remainder of their allotted 12 weeks' after sick leave; under R1e the whole 12-week period counts, because the employer guarantees regular salary with teaching relieved once the employee's own sick leave is used. No qualifying word (R13).
components.relief_note: Non-teaching duties named as continuing: supervising graduate students, graduate committees, administrative duties, committee work, other duties designated by the chair. Teaching is the duty relieved. Research and clinical are not named, so continue (R4b). Category Just teaching (R1e example).

sequence.note: S1: employer pay (salary with teaching relieved) during the FMLA leave, which the institution does not grant as a leave of its own, is linked within the statute; it starts with the leave under R1e (sick leave first, counted in the whole period).

notes: Reference date 2018-02-26. Most UT Arlington HOP and HR procedure texts survive only in 2019-01-03 captures; the documents' version notes direct a version_uncertain flag on every component citing 2018_00, 2018_01, 2018_02, 2018_03, 2018_04, 2018_05 and 2018_07. Regents' Rules 30201 (2016 capture) and 31007 (2017 capture), Procedure 3-61 (2017 capture), the HR FAQs (2017-2018 captures) and the 2015 capture of HOP 6-300 are read as in force.

HOP 6-300: the 2019 capture (2018_03) lists amendments of August 21, 2017 and December 7, 2018 (after the reference date). Its tenure-extension text matches the 2015 capture (2018_13), so 2018_13 is cited for c8 and c9 (version note). HOP 6-352 (2018_02) restates Regents' Rule 31007's guideline without 'birth of a child'; HOP 6-300 is the specific implementing policy and is coded.
2018_08 is an HR index page of links with no policy text.

No paid parental or maternity leave: the FMLA FAQ states 'The University does not have maternity leave as birth/care of newborns falls under FMLA.' The faculty-specific provision is HOP 6-1103 (c1): sick leave first, then either the rest of the 12 FMLA weeks unpaid or non-teaching duties at regular salary; coded as 12 weeks of relief under R1e, which names this provision. The unpaid alternative is the FMLA leave itself (c2), so it is not a separate component; the statute carries no in_lieu_of (R15b).

HOP 6-1103 also creates a Provost-level replacement pay pool to pay substitute instructors (accessed for leave of more than 4 weeks within a consecutive 12-week period); this funds course coverage, not the parent, so it is not a component.

State parental leave (Procedure 3-69; Tex. Gov't Code 661.913; Regents' Rule 30201 Sec. 6): up to 12 weeks unpaid from the birth or placement, sick and vacation leave first, for employees with under 12 months of state service or under 1,250 hours; both parents at UTA share 12 weeks. Under U8 the member described is FMLA-eligible, so this path is recorded in c2's note, not as a component.

Not components (cannot be used for a birth, or not for parents): faculty development leave (HOP 6-1101; Regents' Rule 30201 Sec. 4; Tex. Educ. Code 51.101); the Pre-Tenure Research Reapportionment Program (HOP 6-300/6-310, a fourth-year research award); administrative leave; funeral, jury, voting, firefighter, reserve officer, Red Cross, donor and assistance-dog leaves; foster parent leave (only to attend agency or school meetings for a foster child); holidays; military leaves.

Calendar: HOP 6-300 refers to 'one long semester (i.e., fall or spring)', so the kind of term is the semester; no length is stated, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order. No component is measured in terms.

Documents cited but not saved: Sick Leave Pool (Procedure 3-38); the HOP policy for catastrophic illnesses (HOP 6-1103); the Handbook of Fiscal Regulations and Procedures (HOP 6-1101); the Annual Leave procedure listed on the HR page; 'extended disability leave' (Procedure 3-16, no document named); Request for Family and Medical Leave (Form 3-23); 'Faculty Leave and Related Policies Summary (coming soon)' on the HR page; Regents' Rules 31002, 31006 and 31008 (not leave policies).

Chain, birth parent: FMLA 12 weeks from the birth (c2), with own sick leave drawn first inside it (c3, within c2) and the HOP 6-1103 relief at regular salary, teaching relieved, for the 12 weeks (c1, within c2; R1e); sick leave pool after paid leave is exhausted (c4, consecutive_after c3; discretionary, own balance); then general leave without pay after FMLA expires (c6, consecutive_after c2; general purpose).

Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA 12 weeks (c2) with the HOP 6-1103 relief within it (c1); own sick leave only to care for the spouse recovering from labor and delivery or for an ill child (c3, within c2); then general leave without pay (c6, consecutive_after c2; general purpose).
Conflict noted on c3: HOP 6-1103 bars sick leave for adoption of a healthy child; Procedure 3-10 and Procedure 3-16 allow it for adoption of a child under three. Affects adoptive coding only.
